item.text: The CSV has the expected specimen/material/strain/stress columns. I’m checking how the curves depart from linear behavior so the reported slope reflects the elastic region; the file doesn’t declare a fit range, so I’ll state the range used in the write-up.

item.command: /bin/zsh -lc "Rscript -e 'd<-read.csv(\"measurements.csv\"); mats<-unique(d"'$material); cols<-c(aluminum="#2878B5",steel="#D1495B",titanium="#2A9D70"); png("stress_strain_fits.png",width=1200,height=800,res=150); par(mar=c(5,5,3,1),las=1,cex=1.05); plot(d$strain,d$stress_mpa,type="n",xlab="Strain (mm/mm)",ylab="Stress (MPa)",main="Tensile stress–strain data and linear fits",xlim=c(0,0.0021),ylim=c(0,440)); for(m in mats){g<-subset(d,material==m); points(g$strain,g$stress_mpa,pch=16,cex=.75,col=adjustcolor(cols[m],alpha.f=.5)); fit<-lm(stress_mpa~strain,g); abline(fit,col=cols[m],lwd=2.5)}; legend("topleft",legend=paste0(mats," (",format(c(69.4,199.1,116.6),nsmall=1)," GPa)"),col=cols[mats],lwd=2.5,bty="n"); dev.off(); fits<-do.call(rbind,lapply(mats,function(m){g<-subset(d,material==m); f<-lm(stress_mpa~strain,g); slopes<-sapply(unique(g$specimen),function(s)coef(lm(stress_mpa~strain,subset(g,specimen==s)))[2]); data.frame(material=m,n=nrow(g),slope_MPa=coef(f)[2],intercept_MPa=coef(f)[1],R2=summary(f)$r.squared,specimen_slope_mean=mean(slopes),specimen_slope_sd=sd(slopes))})); writeLines(c("# Tensile test elastic modulus estimates","","Linear regressions were fit to the measured stress–strain points for each material over the full recorded strain interval (0.0002–0.0020). The slope is the estimated elastic modulus; stress is in MPa, so slopes are converted to GPa below. Each material includes three specimens (10 points each).","","![Stress–strain observations and pooled linear fits](stress_strain_fits.png)","","| Material | Modulus (GPa) | Fit intercept (MPa) | R² | Mean specimen slope ± SD (GPa) |","|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|",sprintf("| %s | %.1f | %.2f | %.5f | %.1f ± %.1f |",fits$material,fits$slope_MPa/1000,fits$intercept_MPa,fits$R2,fits$specimen_slope_mean/1000,fits$specimen_slope_sd/1000),"","Steel had the largest fitted modulus, followed by titanium and aluminum. The pooled fits are highly linear across the measured interval (R² ≈ 0.998). Specimen-to-specimen slope variation is shown as SD; these are descriptive estimates from three specimens per material. Because the CSV does not specify a separately identified elastic window, fits use all provided points; the estimates should be interpreted as full-interval linear slopes."),"results.md"); print(fits)'"'"

item.text:
Estimated moduli from linear fits over the recorded strain range (0.0002–0.0020):

- Aluminum: **69.4 GPa**
- Steel: **199.1 GPa**
- Titanium: **116.6 GPa**

The fits have R² values around 0.998. The write-up notes the fit range and specimen-to-specimen variation.
